experiment_description: A periodic first-principles structural and charge-density modeling procedure is applied to monolayer MoS2 as the material platform for testing whether second-order optical responses require many-body correlations beyond two-particle excitons. The target structure is a single S-Mo-S layer in a hexagonal close-packed supercell with one molybdenum plane between two sulfur planes, point group D3h and space group P6m2, with the in-plane lattice parameter fixed to the experimental bulk value 3.16 Å. The out-of-plane supercell height is 20 Å to separate periodically repeated slabs, and slab-geometry Coulomb truncation is used to suppress image interactions. Ground-state DFT is performed in the local-density approximation using QUANTUM ESPRESSO with fully relativistic optimized norm-conserving Vanderbilt SG15 pseudopotentials; molybdenum 4s and 4p semicore states are included as valence along with 4d and 5s states. Self-consistent calculations use fixed occupations, a 12 × 12 in-plane k-point mesh, and a 100 Ry plane-wave cutoff. Atomic coordinates are relaxed until all forces are below 10^-6 Ry/a0 while the in-plane lattice parameter and supercell height are fixed. The spatial-geometric scope is the translationally periodic primitive monolayer unit cell with no finite edges or defects; surface continuity and out-of-plane extent are assessed from the planar, in-plane averaged electron charge density rho(z) along the full 20 Å supercell. The intended goal is to determine the relaxed intrinsic S-Mo-S layer geometry and the effective electronic thickness used to convert supercell optical tensors into 3D-like monolayer quantities.

relaxed_mo_s_plane_separation_A.description: The relaxed vertical separation between the molybdenum plane and each sulfur plane in the monolayer unit cell.

relaxed_mo_s_bond_length_A.description: The relaxed nearest-neighbor Mo-S bond length in the monolayer unit cell.

effective_monolayer_thickness_A.description: The electronic effective monolayer thickness obtained from the out-of-plane extent of the planar-averaged charge density.

experiment_description: The electronic band structure of monolayer MoS2 is calculated to establish the one-particle and quasiparticle electronic starting point for a TDCDFT description of excitonic and trionic contributions to second-harmonic generation. The structure is a periodic S-Mo-S monolayer in a 20 Å out-of-plane supercell with slab Coulomb truncation, fixed in-plane lattice parameter 3.16 Å, relaxed S-Mo-S geometry, and no finite-size edges or defects; the electronic properties are averaged over the full two-dimensional Brillouin zone of the primitive cell. The baseline band dispersion is obtained from LDA DFT in QUANTUM ESPRESSO using fully relativistic SG15 norm-conserving pseudopotentials, Mo semicore states as valence, fixed occupations, a 12 × 12 self-consistent k-point mesh, and a 100 Ry plane-wave cutoff. Quasiparticle corrections are then computed from the LDA wave functions and energies using the one-shot G0W0 approximation in YAMBO. The G0W0 dielectric matrix uses the plasmon-pole approximation, 12 Ry cutoff for the dielectric matrix, 40 Ry cutoff for exchange and correlation self-energy terms, up to 220 bands in dielectric-matrix and correlation sums, the Bruneval-Gonze acceleration for empty states, a 30 × 30 k-point mesh, random-integration of the screened potential with 2 × 10^6 Monte Carlo points, reciprocal-vector cutoffs of 2.5 Ry and 1 Ry for bare and screened Coulomb terms, and slab Coulomb truncation. The band path sampled for reporting is Gamma-K-M-Gamma, and the direct-gap location is identified relative to the high-symmetry points of the monolayer Brillouin zone.

lda_direct_band_gap_eV.description: The direct electronic band gap from the LDA band structure.

g0w0_direct_band_gap_eV.description: The direct quasiparticle band gap after one-shot G0W0 correction.

direct_gap_k_point.description: The Brillouin-zone high-symmetry point at which the direct valence-to-conduction gap occurs.

experiment_description: The linear optical response of monolayer MoS2 is computed as the two-particle excitonic input for the paper's central TDCDFT strategy: a dynamical long-range linear exchange-correlation kernel is constructed so that second-harmonic generation can include electron-hole excitonic screening before testing three-particle trionic corrections. The sample model is a pristine, translationally periodic monolayer MoS2 primitive cell in a 20 Å slab supercell with fixed in-plane lattice parameter 3.16 Å, relaxed S-Mo-S geometry, slab Coulomb truncation, and optical tensors rescaled using an effective monolayer thickness of 7.3 Å; the spatial scope is the full periodic monolayer, with response averaged over the unit cell and sampled over the two-dimensional Brillouin zone. Starting from LDA wave functions and G0W0 quasiparticle energies computed with the settings specified for the quasiparticle calculation, the Bethe-Salpeter equation is solved in YAMBO using the Lanczos-Haydock solver. The BSE kernel uses 25 Ry cutoff for the electron-hole exchange part and 8 Ry cutoff for the electron-hole attraction part; 14 occupied and 22 unoccupied spin-split states are included in the excitonic Hamiltonian; a 33 × 33 k-point mesh is used. The optical observable is the in-plane xx component of the macroscopic dielectric function over photon energies from 0 to 5 eV, including spin-orbit effects and electron-hole attraction. Peak positions are read from the computed macroscopic optical dielectric spectrum.

a_b_exciton_doublet_energy_lower_eV.description: The lower photon-energy bound of the A/B exciton double-peak region in the BSE macroscopic optical dielectric spectrum.

a_b_exciton_doublet_energy_upper_eV.description: The upper photon-energy bound of the A/B exciton double-peak region in the BSE macroscopic optical dielectric spectrum.

c_exciton_peak_energy_eV.description: The photon energy of the C excitonic peak in the BSE macroscopic optical dielectric spectrum.

experiment_description: A frequency-dependent in-plane long-range linear exchange-correlation screening tensor is extracted for monolayer MoS2 to encode two-particle electron-hole excitonic effects inside the TDCDFT formulation of second-harmonic generation. The calculation uses the pristine periodic monolayer geometry in a 20 Å slab supercell with in-plane lattice parameter 3.16 Å, relaxed S-Mo-S coordinates, slab Coulomb truncation, and monolayer tensor rescaling using effective thickness 7.3 Å. The spatial scope is the homogeneous primitive monolayer unit cell averaged macroscopically, with reciprocal-space sampling over the two-dimensional Brillouin zone; no finite edges, grains, or local defects are included. The independent-particle/random-phase optical dielectric tensor epsilon_RPA(omega) is obtained without electron-hole attraction, while epsilon_BSE(omega) is obtained from the Bethe-Salpeter calculation including excitonic effects. Here omega denotes the optical photon angular frequency expressed on the plotted energy axis in eV; A_LRC(omega) denotes the tensorial long-range linear exchange-correlation screening parameter; epsilon_BSE(omega) and epsilon_RPA(omega) are optical dielectric tensors; the superscript -1 denotes tensor inverse; subtraction and multiplication are tensor operations; and the reported component is the in-plane xx component allowed by D3h symmetry. The frequency window is 0 to 5 eV, matching the optical dielectric calculation.

linear_lrc_screening_tensor_formula.description: The tensor relation used to extract the dynamical linear long-range exchange-correlation screening tensor from BSE and RPA optical dielectric tensors.

experiment_description: The second-harmonic-generation response of monolayer MoS2 is computed with many-body effects included up to the two-particle excitonic level, to test the baseline part of the paper's central claim that excitons alone do not fully determine the quantitative nonlinear optical response. The modeled material is pristine periodic monolayer MoS2 with D3h symmetry, fixed in-plane lattice parameter 3.16 Å, relaxed S-Mo-S geometry, a 20 Å slab supercell, slab Coulomb truncation, and optical response rescaled using effective layer thickness Leff = 7.3 Å. The geometric scope is the homogeneous monolayer primitive cell with no finite edges or defects; the macroscopic xxy susceptibility is obtained by averaging the microscopic interacting optical polarizability over the unit cell and integrating over the full two-dimensional Brillouin zone. Independent-particle SHG tensors are evaluated in the optical and long-wavelength limit using length-gauge expressions implemented in WANNIER90. The Wannier interpolation starts from 48 spin-split bands and constructs 36 disentangled maximally localized Wannier functions spanning 14 high-energy valence bands and 22 low-energy conduction bands, using two p trial orbitals on S atoms and one s plus one d trial orbital on the Mo atom. The interpolated k-point mesh is 1000 × 1000, the imaginary broadening of hbar*omega is eta = 0.1 eV, the denominator regularization parameter is eta_r = 0.05 eV, and occupation factors and derivatives are evaluated at T = 0 K. The photon energy omega is swept from 0.50 to 2.50 eV for the SHG process in which two photons of frequency omega generate radiation at 2omega. The interacting TDCDFT calculation uses the dynamical linear long-range kernel A_LRC(omega) extracted from the BSE optical dielectric tensor, while the quadratic long-range kernel is fixed to B_LRC^xxy = 0 a.u., so that three-particle trionic correlations are not included. The reported observable is the absolute two-dimensional SHG susceptibility component |chi_2^xxy(omega,omega)| multiplied by Leff, in nm^2/V.

two_particle_shg_onset_energy_eV.description: The photon energy at which the calculated excitonic-only SHG signal begins in the swept spectrum.

two_particle_shg_first_resonance_energy_.description: The photon energy of the first pronounced resonance in the calculated excitonic-only SHG spectrum.

two_particle_shg_peak_susceptibility_nm2.description: The peak value of the calculated excitonic-only absolute two-dimensional xxy SHG susceptibility in the main resonance region.

experiment_description: The second-harmonic-generation response of monolayer MoS2 is recalculated while sweeping a static long-range quadratic exchange-correlation screening tensor to parameterize three-particle trionic correlations, which is the central mechanism proposed in the paper for improving quantitative nonlinear optical predictions beyond an exciton-only treatment. The material model, spatial averaging, and numerical SHG workflow are the same as for the excitonic-only SHG calculation: pristine periodic monolayer MoS2 with D3h symmetry, in-plane lattice parameter 3.16 Å, relaxed S-Mo-S geometry, 20 Å slab supercell, slab Coulomb truncation, Leff = 7.3 Å monolayer rescaling, length-gauge independent-particle response in WANNIER90, 36 maximally localized Wannier functions spanning 14 valence and 22 conduction bands from 48 spin-split bands, 1000 × 1000 interpolated k-point mesh, eta = 0.1 eV optical broadening, eta_r = 0.05 eV denominator regularization, and T = 0 K occupations. The SHG process is omega + omega -> 2omega with photon energy omega swept across 0.50 to 2.50 eV. The dynamical linear kernel A_LRC(omega) is retained to include two-particle excitonic screening, while the in-plane longitudinal quadratic component B_LRC^xxy is swept from -4 to 0 atomic units. For each value of B_LRC^xxy, the height of the main |chi_2^xxy(omega,omega)| × Leff peak near the C-exciton-related SHG resonance is computed and compared with the reference peak height from the reported monolayer MoS2 SHG spectrum used for calibration.

optimal_quadratic_lrc_screening_paramete.description: The fitted static in-plane xxy quadratic long-range exchange-correlation screening parameter associated with trionic three-particle correlations.

quadratic_lrc_sweep_peak_reduction_facto.description: The approximate factor by which the main SHG peak height is reduced across the negative quadratic-kernel range relative to the excitonic-only calculation.

experiment_description: A trion-corrected second-harmonic-generation spectrum is computed for monolayer MoS2 using the static quadratic long-range exchange-correlation tensor value selected from the B_LRC^xxy sweep, in order to characterize the nonlinear optical response when both two-particle excitonic and three-particle trionic correlations are included in the TDCDFT response. The material model is the pristine periodic monolayer MoS2 primitive cell with D3h symmetry, fixed in-plane lattice parameter 3.16 Å, relaxed S-Mo-S coordinates, a 20 Å slab supercell, slab Coulomb truncation, and effective thickness Leff = 7.3 Å for converting the supercell response to a two-dimensional susceptibility. The response is a macroscopic unit-cell average over the homogeneous monolayer and a Brillouin-zone integral over a 1000 × 1000 interpolated mesh; finite edges, substrate disorder, and local defects are not part of the model. Independent-particle SHG tensors are calculated in the optical long-wavelength limit using WANNIER90 length-gauge expressions with 36 maximally localized Wannier functions obtained from 48 spin-split bands, spanning 14 valence and 22 conduction bands; eta = 0.1 eV, eta_r = 0.05 eV, and T = 0 K are used. The interacting TDCDFT response uses the BSE-derived dynamical linear A_LRC(omega) and a static quadratic component B_LRC^xxy = -3.5 a.u. The photon energy omega is swept from 0.50 to 2.50 eV for the SHG process omega + omega -> 2omega, and the reported output is |chi_2^xxy(omega,omega)| × Leff in nm^2/V.

trion_corrected_main_shg_peak_energy_eV.description: The photon energy of the main SHG peak when the static quadratic trionic kernel is included.

trion_corrected_main_shg_peak_susceptibi.description: The main-peak value of the absolute two-dimensional xxy SHG susceptibility when the static quadratic trionic kernel is included.
